body.text: Bariatric surgery requires tighter logistical discipline than minor outpatient procedures because you are recovering from abdominal incisions, general anaesthesia, and a strict liquid hydration protocol. [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) is an independent, client-paid, flat-fee travel and medical travel advisory run by its two founders in Türkiye—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions. We align your hospital-to-hotel transfers, recovery room setup, and airport assistance around the clinical schedule set by your surgical team.
What pre-op cardiology, endoscopy and lab checks happen on Day 1?

Day 1 is dedicated to hospital-based pre-operative clearance: fasting blood panels, chest imaging, abdominal ultrasound, an electrocardiogram (ECG) with a cardiologist, a pulmonology or anaesthesia review, and often an upper GI endoscopy to inspect the stomach lining and check for hiatal hernia or gastritis before surgery.

These diagnostics confirm you are safe for general anaesthesia and laparoscopic resection. Under the [Turkish Ministry of Health Regulation on International Health Tourism](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-108974/regulation-on-international-health-tourism-and-tourist-health.html), hospitals admitting international patients must hold valid authorization, and you can confirm a facility's listing on the [Ministry of Health authorized providers directory](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html). Plan to arrive fasting as instructed by your hospital, and keep Day 1 free of sightseeing so results can be reviewed promptly.

body.text: What happens during Hospital Days 2–4 including the leak test?

On Day 2, your surgeon performs the laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy and nurses encourage short walks within hours to stimulate circulation. On Day 3, your team typically runs a staple-line leak test—using oral methylene blue dye or contrast imaging—before clearing you to sip clear liquids, leading to hospital discharge on Day 4.

According to [Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/sleeve-gastrectomy/about/pac-20385183), laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy involves smaller incisions and a short inpatient monitoring window, commonly one to two nights domestically, though international protocols in Türkiye typically extend inpatient observation to two or three nights before hotel transfer. Never rush discharge if your surgeon recommends an extra night for hydration or nausea control.
How do Hotel Days 5–6 and final discharge work?

Hotel Days 5 and 6 bridge the gap between inpatient nursing and commercial air travel. You stay within 15 to 25 minutes of the hospital, follow a strict clear-liquid sipping schedule, take short hourly walks in the corridor, and attend a final surgeon review on Day 6 for wound inspection and written travel clearance.

Through our [medical tourism coordination service](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism), we match bariatric patients with hotels that offer ground-level entry or reliable lifts, walk-in showers, and kitchens willing to provide plain clear broths and decaffeinated herbal teas. Your final discharge pack should include your operative report, pathology or endoscopy notes, medication schedule, and dietitian progression guide in English.
What luggage and flight rules apply on Day 7?

On Day 7, avoid lifting any suitcase heavier than a few kilograms to protect abdominal incisions, pre-book airport wheelchair assistance to avoid long terminal walks, and follow strict deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention steps during the flight—including compression stockings, aisle-seat mobility, and steady small sips of water.

Recent surgery combined with prolonged sitting raises blood clot risk. The [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/blood-clots/risk-factors/travel.html) and [NHS](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/deep-vein-thrombosis-dvt/) emphasize staying hydrated, flexing calf muscles, and walking regularly during travel, while the [CDC Yellow Book](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/travel-air-sea/deep-vein-thrombosis-and-pulmonary-embolism.html) details aviation thrombosis precautions. Ask your surgeon whether blood-thinning injections or stockings are required for your specific flight duration—especially on long-haul routes over four hours.

items: Zero heavy lifting: Check your main bag with porter help or travel with a companion; carry only a light personal sling bag.
Wheelchair request (WCHR): Submit airline special assistance at least 48 hours before departure so you skip long walks at Istanbul Airport.
Aisle seat selection: Choose an aisle seat to stand and stretch every 60 to 90 minutes when the seatbelt sign is off.
Measured hydration: Bring an empty wide-mouth bottle to fill airside and sip water slowly; skip carbonated drinks and straws.
Carry clinical paperwork: Keep your fit-to-fly certificate, operative summary, and prescribed anticoagulant injections (with prescription letter) in your hand luggage.

faq.q: Is 7 days always enough for gastric sleeve surgery in Türkiye?
faq.a: Seven days covers the standard uncomplicated timeline, but travellers taking long-haul flights (8+ hours) or managing additional health conditions often benefit from adding two extra hotel nights for rest before flying.

faq.q: What happens if my Day 1 endoscopy finds gastritis or an ulcer?
faq.a: Your licensed surgical team decides whether to proceed, prescribe short-term medication, or postpone surgery. Always book changeable return flights and flexible hotel rates in case clinical findings adjust your dates.

faq.q: Can I drink normal amounts of water on the plane home?
faq.a: No. After a sleeve gastrectomy, your stomach volume is greatly reduced, so you must take small, steady sips throughout the flight rather than gulping fluids. Follow the exact fluid targets set by your bariatric dietitian.

faq.q: How should I carry blood-thinning injections through airport security?
faq.a: Pack prescribed syringes in their original labelled box inside your cabin bag alongside an English doctor's letter stating medical necessity. Declare them at the airport security screening tray.

faq.q: Can I travel solo for gastric sleeve surgery?
faq.a: Some patients travel solo using private hospital transfers and pre-booked airport assistance, though having a companion helps with luggage handling, pharmacy runs, and comfort on Days 2 to 5.
